# A Workspace born headless arms the wrong window and never projects

## Context

Measured live on `apps/workstation` at `dev@2ee23d7801` (blob `115a3f9b98`) through the Neural Link while running the D#18224 popup-birth arm ([receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/18224#discussioncomment-18289525)). `Neo.create('Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace', {dockModel})` with no parent and no window succeeds, does two wrong things, and one of them is silent. Every shipping host hides both by seeding a first shell in its own constructor — knowledge only the engine has, which is this epic's theme.

Filed at the operator's request to capture the arm's findings as engine work; the D#18224 Step-Back (DC_kwDODSospM4BFxQB, addendum) lists the same two requirements as acceptance criteria of the owner design, so this leaf is prerequisite work for it, not part of its vehicle decision.

## The Problem

1. **Construct arms geometry on a window it does not have.** `construct` calls `observeWindowGeometry(this.windowId)` unconditionally (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:548`). With `windowId: null` the remote call carries no routing key; `src/worker/Base.mjs:478–484` delivers it to `ports[0]` and the worker console prints `sendMessage destination "main" is deprecated … remoteMethod: setConfigs, data: {observeMovement: true, observeResize: true, windowId: null}`. `WindowPosition#setConfigs` (`src/main/addon/WindowPosition.mjs:330`) deletes `data.windowId`, so nothing is poisoned — but an arbitrary window was armed by a workspace that has no render target.
2. **The class owns no first projection, and the failure is silent.** After binding (`Neo.worker.App#moveComponent` into a viewport → `container.Base#createItem` NeoInstance branch, `:413–437`, adopts `windowId`/`appName`, `mounted: true`), `onDockZoneDocumentChange(document)` renders nothing: `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` throws `Dock projection could not find a current shell at index 0` (`src/dashboard/dock/projection/Reconciler.mjs:353–357`), the error is untyped, `onDockProjectionFailed` re-throws it (`Workspace.mjs:3923`), and the rejected `refreshPromise` reaches no console. (A rejected refresh tail was left outside #18039's fixed scope on purpose; this leaf adds no generic logging either — it makes the no-shell state not an error.) `examples/dashboard/dock/MainContainer.mjs:147, :310` and every host seed `items = [projectDockModel()]` in `construct`, which is why nobody sees it.

Seeded through a hot-patched `beforeRefreshDockWorkspace` (`this.add(this.projectDockModel(null, null, document))` when no shell exists), the same instance projected its document, and with a registry-answered `resolvePane` adopted two LIVE panes of the main workspace by projection alone (same ids, `verify_component_consistency` 1/1/1).

## The Architectural Reality

- `construct` `:516–549`: preview producer, optional tear-out handlers + worker `connect`/`disconnect` subscription (`:535`), then the unconditional geometry arm (`:548`).
- `refreshDockWorkspace` `:3741` waits for the host to mount, then projects and reconciles; the reconciler requires `host.items[shellIndex]` to exist (`:353–357`).
- `onDockProjectionFailed` `:3918–3949` recovers only errors marked `isDockProjectionFailure`; everything else re-throws into the refresh tail.
- ADR 0029 §2.1: the workspace container owns the committed document and re-projects it through `LayoutAdapter.project()` — the first projection is part of that contract, not the consumer's.

## The Fix

> **Narrowed 2026-09-04 14:55Z per intake ([IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABSlARkA](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18276#issuecomment-5541728656)), verified against `Reconciler.mjs:353–399` and `Workspace.mjs:2074`:** once this leaf lands, "no current shell" is the first projection's **precondition**, not a projection failure. Typing the no-shell throw as recoverable would retry against the same missing shell; with a seed present the typed error would be unreachable.

1. Guard the geometry arm on a window: one idempotent window-binding hook arms only a real, newly bound `windowId` (`afterSetWindowId` from `null` to an id); `construct` calls the same guarded helper, so a headless instance arms nothing — beside `component/Abstract#afterSetWindowId` `:289–304` (theme files) and `component/Base#afterSetWindowId` `:959–962` (drag zones).
2. Own the first projection as the normal path: `Workspace#afterSetMounted` (`:2074`) detects an absent shell at `dockShellIndex` and schedules the ordinary document refresh; `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` treats `oldShell === null` (`:353`) as an explicit **first projection** — mount exactly one shell at `shellIndex`, resolve its panes, make it visible, return a normal result with `landedInPlace: false` (`:394–399` vocabulary) — never staging beside a shell that does not exist. Consumers that already supply a shell keep their static boot path.
3. Only a failing initial mount is a failure: if the first projection's mount or reconciliation rejects, retire the failed initial shell back to zero shells and mark the real error as a typed projection failure with the named recovery `retired-initial`, so the existing exactly-one retry rule of `onDockProjectionFailed` operates on it. Generic refresh-tail logging stays out of this leaf.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Workspace#construct` geometry arm (`:548`) | ADR 0029 §2.8.5 (the host arms its own render target) | arms only with a `windowId`; a headless instance arms nothing | none needed | class docblock | worker console shows no deprecated-destination warning on `Neo.create(Workspace, {dockModel})` |
| `Workspace#afterSetWindowId` (inherited) + `afterSetMounted` (`:2074`) | `component/Abstract:289` cascade | first bind arms geometry once (idempotent, real id only); the mount schedules the first projection | — | class docblock | headless → bind renders the document with no consumer seeding |
| `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` with `oldShell === null` (`:353–357`) | ADR 0029 §2.1 (the workspace owns projection) | explicit first projection: one shell mounted at `shellIndex`, `landedInPlace: false`; a rejected initial mount retires to zero shells and surfaces as a typed failure with recovery `retired-initial` | current untyped throw | Reconciler docblock | headless → bind renders; a forced initial-mount rejection surfaces once and retries once |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` §2.1 / §2.8.5 — no authority changes; the leaf makes the class honour a contract it already states.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit: `Neo.create(Workspace, {dockModel})` with no window emits no remote geometry call (spy on `Neo.main.addon.WindowPosition.setConfigs`), and binding it into a container with a `windowId` arms exactly one.
- [ ] Unit: after `viewport.add(headlessWorkspace)` and `onDockZoneDocumentChange(document)`, the host holds one shell projecting the document's tabs nodes — no consumer seeding, no hot patch.
- [ ] Unit, red-first at `dev@2ee23d7801`: the same sequence today leaves `items` empty and `refreshPromise` rejected with the untyped no-shell error.
- [ ] The no-shell precondition never produces a failure; a first projection whose initial mount rejects (forced in the spec) retires the initial shell back to zero shells, fires `dockProjectionFailed` with recovery `retired-initial`, and retries exactly once — never a silent rejection.
- [ ] `examples/dashboard/dock/MainContainer.mjs` keeps working with its constructor seeding removed (deletion, per the accretion rule), and the Workstation is unchanged.

## Out of Scope

- The owner-level item→instance registry (the D#18224 owner design; the arm faked it with `Neo.getComponent(componentRef)`).
- Moving the tear-out lifecycle out of `Workspace` (D#18150 cluster 1).
- Popup-birth latency (needs the Playwright rig; separate arm).

## Avoided Traps

- Projecting in `construct`: a headless instance must project nothing (Step-Back addendum: headless arms neither geometry nor visible projection); the first projection belongs to the first bind.
- Typing the no-shell throw as a recoverable failure: the retry would run against the same missing shell, and with a seed present the typed error is unreachable (intake correction). Only a failing initial mount is a failure; other throws stay loud.
- Reviving generic refresh-tail logging here: #18039 left it out explicitly; it needs its own evidence and owner.

## Ticket intake — `needs-narrowing`; implementation held on one contract correction

The live arm and current source at `origin/dev@205bc52f8a` confirm both root facts:

1. `Workspace#construct` calls `observeWindowGeometry(null)`, which routes through the deprecated default-port fallback.
2. `Reconciler.reconcileProjection()` rejects before doing any work when `host.items[shellIndex]` is absent, so a bound headless Workspace has no engine-owned first projection.

The goal is high-ROI and aligned with ADR 0029. The current recovery prescription, however, makes the new normal state an error.

### `[ARCH_ALIGNMENT]` — narrow the first-projection/recovery contract

Once this leaf supports a Workspace with no old shell, **“no current shell” is the successful first-projection precondition**, not a projection failure. Merely marking today’s no-shell throw as `isDockProjectionFailure` and routing it through `onDockProjectionFailed()` schedules one clean retry against the same missing shell; without a separate seed it fails twice, and with a separate seed the typed error is unreachable.

The coherent contract is:

1. `Workspace#afterSetMounted` detects an absent shell and schedules the normal document refresh; consumers that already supplied a shell keep their current static boot path.
2. `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` treats `oldShell === null` as an explicit **first projection**: mount exactly one shell at `shellIndex`, resolve its panes, make it visible, and return a normal `landedInPlace: false` result. It must not stage “beside” an old shell that does not exist.
3. If that initial mount/reconciliation itself rejects, retire the failed initial shell back to zero shells, mark the real error as a typed projection failure with a named recovery such as `retired-initial`, and let the existing exactly-one retry rule operate.
4. Keep generic refresh-tail logging out of this leaf. `onDockProjectionFailed` already logs typed failures. The “any rejected refresh logs once” concern was explicitly left outside `#18039`; it needs its own evidence/owner if revived.

Please update the third Fix row, the Reconciler Contract-Ledger row, AC-3/AC-4, and the related `#18039` wording to encode that distinction. The geometry half can remain: an idempotent Workspace window-binding hook should arm only a real, newly bound `windowId`, while `construct` may call the same guarded helper.

## Ticket intake follow-up — `valid-as-written`

The author’s 14:55Z body edit discharges the prior `needs-narrowing` verdict. Current source at `origin/dev@57ae8880e4` still has both measured failures: `Workspace#construct` arms geometry with an unguarded `windowId`, and `Reconciler.reconcileProjection()` throws before it can create a first shell. No PR closes #18276 and the semantic duplicate sweep found no equivalent.

The corrected prescription is coherent: no shell is the normal first-projection precondition; exactly one shell is mounted at `dockShellIndex`; only a rejected initial mount becomes typed `retired-initial` recovery and spends the existing one-retry budget. Generic refresh logging remains excluded.

### Scope boundary on the later unbind note

Do **not** pair the bind hook with `WindowPosition.setConfigs({observeMovement: false, observeResize: false, windowId: oldValue})` in this leaf. Live source shows those flags are realm-global addon configs: `setConfigs()` deletes `windowId` and applies `this.set(data)`; there is no Workspace-keyed lease or refcount. One Workspace unbinding could therefore silence a geometry stream another consumer still needs. #18276 should arm a real newly bound window id and suppress the headless arm, exactly as its body says. Retained-headless release belongs with a future owner/refcount contract, not a bare inverse write.
